findings.location: Product price labels (e.g., '£17.46', '£23.88') and 'In stock' availability text
findings.issue: The bright green color used for the price and stock status text has insufficient contrast against the white background, falling below the WCAG AA requirement of 4.5:1.
findings.user_impact: Users with moderate visual impairments or those viewing the site on low-contrast screens will struggle to read price and availability information.
findings.recommendation: Change the text color to a darker green (e.g., #2b701a) to achieve a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the white background.

findings.location: Product title links (e.g., 'Set Me Free', 'Olio', 'Libertarianism for Beginners')
findings.issue: The light blue color of the product title links has an estimated contrast ratio of 2.7:1 against the white background, which fails the WCAG AA minimum contrast requirement of 4.5:1.
findings.user_impact: Visually impaired users will have difficulty identifying and reading the names of the books in the store grid.
findings.recommendation: Darken the link text color to a compliant shade of blue (e.g., #1a5c96) that meets the 4.5:1 contrast ratio requirement.

findings.location: 'Add to basket' button for 'Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little...' (Row 1, Column 2)
findings.issue: The background color of this button is a darker shade of blue than all other active 'Add to basket' buttons on the page, creating an unexplained inconsistency in the interface.
findings.user_impact: Users might be confused about whether this product is in a different state (e.g., selected or hovered) compared to the others, leading to interface uncertainty.
findings.recommendation: Ensure all standard product buttons use the identical blue color token (e.g., #428bca) to maintain consistency across the catalog grid.

findings.location: Truncated product titles (e.g., 'Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little...', 'Mesaerion: The Best Science...')
findings.issue: The text truncation logic wraps the trailing ellipsis ('...') onto a new line on its own, which looks broken and inconsistent with standard text truncation patterns.
findings.user_impact: It degrades the aesthetic professionalism of the catalog grid and makes the UI look unpolished.
findings.recommendation: Apply CSS properties like `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical;` to handle multi-line truncation gracefully without wrapping the ellipsis alone.
